correctness.rationale: For every n>=1, loopless nonnegative weighted digraph and 0<=lambda<=1, co-singleton inequalities sum to lambda*W <= (3lambda-1)*W, excluding lambda<1/2 when W>0. At lambda=1/2 their coordinate bounds force the sole allocation I/2. For lambda>=1/2 the displayed allocation I/2+(lambda-1/2)O has exact nonnegative slack (lambda-1/2)(A+B)+(1-lambda)(B-E); above the threshold tight coalitions are precisely unions of weak positive-support components, yielding dimension n-c. Explicit restricted allocations prove all restricted cores nonempty above threshold, and the two-node arc is sharp. Zero-weight networks give the zero game. The standalone exact rational program completed 22,085 tests; finite tests are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The source paper expressly invites a weighted internal/external trust-game analysis. The all-network half-weight threshold identifies a universal stability failure as exposure dominates, an isolated unique allocation at balance, and precisely n-c degrees of bargaining freedom when internal interactions dominate. Total balancedness changes at the same sharp threshold. These are structural and graph-topological outputs with a two-peer tight example, not arbitrary computed slices.
